claim: Interactions between the bone marrow (BM) stroma and hematopoietic progenitors contribute to bone-BM homeostasis in mammals.
source: In mammals, interactions between the bone marrow (BM) stroma and hematopoietic progenitors contribute to bone-BM homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data from this manuscript.

claim: Perinatal bone growth and ossification provide a microenvironment for the transition to definitive hematopoiesis.
source: Perinatal bone growth and ossification provide a microenvironment for the transition to definitive hematopoiesis
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: O-GlcNAcylation promotes osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs by modifying and activating RUNX2.
source: By modifying and activating RUNX2, O-GlcNAcylation promotes osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and stromal IL-7 expression to support lymphopoiesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2, including luciferase assays, differentiation assays, and O-GlcNAc site mutations.

claim: O-GlcNAcylation promotes stromal IL-7 expression to support lymphopoiesis.
source: By modifying and activating RUNX2, O-GlcNAcylation promotes osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and stromal IL-7 expression to support lymphopoiesis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 6 showing Il7 gene expression changes with O-GlcNAcylation modulation.

claim: C/EBPβ-dependent marrow adipogenesis is inhibited by O-GlcNAcylation.
source: In contrast, C/EBPβ-dependent marrow adipogenesis and expression of myelopoietic stem cell factor (SCF) is inhibited by O-GlcNAcylation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 4 showing increased adipogenesis in Ogt cKO mice and with OGT inhibition.

claim: Expression of myelopoietic stem cell factor (SCF) is inhibited by O-GlcNAcylation.
source: In contrast, C/EBPβ-dependent marrow adipogenesis and expression of myelopoietic stem cell factor (SCF) is inhibited by O-GlcNAcylation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 6 showing Kitl gene expression changes with O-GlcNAcylation modulation.

claim: Ablating O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) in BMSCs leads to impaired bone formation in mice.
source: Ablating O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) in BMSCs leads to impaired bone formation, increased marrow adiposity, as well as defective B-cell lymphopoiesis and myeloid overproduction in mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 1 showing reduced bone volume and mineralization in Ogt cKO mice.

claim: Ablating O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) in BMSCs leads to increased marrow adiposity in mice.
source: Ablating O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) in BMSCs leads to impaired bone formation, increased marrow adiposity, as well as defective B-cell lymphopoiesis and myeloid overproduction in mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 4 showing massive accumulation of adipocytes in Ogt cKO mice.

claim: Ablating O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) in BMSCs leads to defective B-cell lymphopoiesis in mice.
source: Ablating O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) in BMSCs leads to impaired bone formation, increased marrow adiposity, as well as defective B-cell lymphopoiesis and myeloid overproduction in mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 5 showing reduced B cell populations in Ogt cKO mice.

claim: Ablating O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) in BMSCs leads to myeloid overproduction in mice.
source: Ablating O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) in BMSCs leads to impaired bone formation, increased marrow adiposity, as well as defective B-cell lymphopoiesis and myeloid overproduction in mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 5 showing increased CMP/CLP ratio and increased neutrophils in Ogt cKO mice.

claim: Most bones in mammals are formed through endochondral ossification.
source: Most bones in mammals are formed through endochondral ossification, which is initiated by mesenchymal condensation, followed by the differentiation of chondrocytes and perichondrial progenitors (Kobayashi and Kronenberg, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kobayashi and Kronenberg, 2021.

claim: Endochondral ossification is initiated by mesenchymal condensation, followed by the differentiation of chondrocytes and perichondrial progenitors.
source: Most bones in mammals are formed through endochondral ossification, which is initiated by mesenchymal condensation, followed by the differentiation of chondrocytes and perichondrial progenitors (Kobayashi and Kronenberg, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kobayashi and Kronenberg, 2021.

claim: Perichondrial progenitors expressing Osterix co-migrate with blood vessels into the primary ossification center.
source: Perichondrial progenitors expressing Osterix (encoded by the Sp7 gene) co-migrate with blood vessels into the primary ossification center, giving rise to osteoblasts and transient stromal cells in the nascent BM cavity (Chen et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2013; Maes et al., 2010; Mizoguchi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2013; Maes et al., 2010; Mizoguchi et al., 2014.

claim: Perichondrial progenitors expressing Osterix give rise to osteoblasts and transient stromal cells in the nascent BM cavity.
source: Perichondrial progenitors expressing Osterix (encoded by the Sp7 gene) co-migrate with blood vessels into the primary ossification center, giving rise to osteoblasts and transient stromal cells in the nascent BM cavity (Chen et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2013; Maes et al., 2010; Mizoguchi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2013; Maes et al., 2010; Mizoguchi et al., 2014.

claim: At the perinatal stage, Osterix+ progenitors contribute to osteo-lineages and long-lived BM stromal cells (BMSCs) that exhibit trilineage differentiation potential into osteocytes, chondrocytes, and adipocytes.
source: At the perinatal stage, Osterix+ progenitors contribute to osteo-lineages and long-lived BM stromal cells (BMSCs) that exhibit trilineage differentiation potential into osteocytes, chondrocytes, and adipocytes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The decision of BMSC fate is controlled by a transcriptional network of pro-osteogenic and anti-adipogenic transcription factors that pre-establishes osteogenic enhancers in BMSCs for rapid bone formation.
source: The decision of BMSC fate is controlled by a transcriptional network of pro-osteogenic and anti-adipogenic transcription factors that pre-establishes osteogenic enhancers in BMSCs for rapid bone formation (Rauch et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rauch et al., 2019.

claim: RUNX2 determines the osteoblast lineage from the multipotent BMSCs by regulating osteogenic genes including Sp7.
source: RUNX family transcription factor 2 (RUNX2), by regulating osteogenic genes including Sp7, determines the osteoblast lineage from the multipotent BMSCs.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Mice with Runx2 mutations completely lack skeletal ossification and die of respiratory failure.
source: Mice with Runx2 mutations completely lack skeletal ossification and die of respiratory failure (Komori et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Komori et al., 1997.

claim: Runx2-haploinsufficient mice show specific skeletal abnormalities characteristic of human cleidocranial dysplasia (CCD), including persistent fontanels, delayed closure of cranial sutures, rudimentary clavicles, and dental abnormalities.
source: Runx2-haploinsufficient mice show specific skeletal abnormalities characteristic of human cleidocranial dysplasia (CCD), including persistent fontanels, delayed closure of cranial sutures, rudimentary clavicles, and dental abnormalities (Otto et al., 1997; Takarada et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Otto et al., 1997; Takarada et al., 2016.

claim: Adipogenesis is driven by downregulation of pro-osteogenic factors, remodeling of the chromatin, and activation of adipogenic transcription factors, such as C/EBPs and PPARγ.
source: On the other hand, adipogenesis is driven by downregulation of pro-osteogenic factors, remodeling of the chromatin, and activation of adipogenic transcription factors, such as C/EBPs and PPARγ (Aaron et al., 2021; Rauch et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Aaron et al., 2021; Rauch et al., 2019.

claim: BM adiposity is associated with bone loss in osteoporosis caused by aging, menopause, and anorexia nervosa.
source: BM adiposity is associated with bone loss in osteoporosis caused by aging, menopause, and anorexia nervosa (Bethel et al., 2013; Fazeli et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2015; Scheller et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bethel et al., 2013; Fazeli et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2015; Scheller et al., 2016.

claim: BMSCs and their lineage-differentiated progeny (e.g. osteoblasts and adipocytes) provide a niche microenvironment for hematopoiesis.
source: BMSCs and their lineage-differentiated progeny (e.g. osteoblasts and adipocytes) provide a niche microenvironment for hematopoiesis (Bianco and Robey, 2015; Calvi and Link, 2015; Morrison and Scadden, 2014; Wei and Frenette, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bianco and Robey, 2015; Calvi and Link, 2015; Morrison and Scadden, 2014; Wei and Frenette, 2018.

claim: BMSC-derived stem cell factor (SCF, encoded by the Kitl gene) and CXCL12 are required for the maintenance and differentiation of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs).
source: For example, BMSC-derived stem cell factor (SCF, encoded by the Kitl gene) and CXC chemokine ligand 12 (CXCL12) are required for the maintenance and differentiation of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs) (Asada et al., 2017; Ding et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Asada et al., 2017; Ding et al., 2012.

claim: A prominent subpopulation of perivascular BMSCs express adipocyte markers.
source: A prominent subpopulation of perivascular BMSCs express adipocyte markers (Dolgalev and Tikhonova, 2021; Zhong et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2017), and support steady-state and metabolic-stressed myelopoiesis by secreting SCF (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dolgalev and Tikhonova, 2021; Zhong et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2017.

claim: Perivascular BMSCs expressing adipocyte markers support steady-state and metabolic-stressed myelopoiesis by secreting SCF.
source: A prominent subpopulation of perivascular BMSCs express adipocyte markers (Dolgalev and Tikhonova, 2021; Zhong et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2017), and support steady-state and metabolic-stressed myelopoiesis by secreting SCF (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2019.

claim: Osteolineage cells are crucial for lymphopoiesis.
source: Meanwhile, osteolineage cells are crucial for lymphopoiesis (Wei and Frenette, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wei and Frenette, 2018.

claim: Depleting Osterix+ cells halts B cell maturation and causes immune failure.
source: Depleting Osterix+ cells halts B cell maturation and causes immune failure (Yu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yu et al., 2016.

claim: IL-7 is the most crucial factor for lymphoid progenitors and is expressed by a subset of BMSCs.
source: IL-7, the most crucial factor for lymphoid progenitors, is expressed by a subset of BMSCs (Fistonich et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fistonich et al., 2018.

claim: Post-translational modifications (PTMs), including phosphorylation, acetylation, and ubiquitination, allow the precise regulation of stability, localization, and activity of BM transcriptional factors, such as RUNX2.
source: Post-translational modifications (PTMs), including phosphorylation, acetylation, and ubiquitination, allow the precise regulation of stability, localization, and activity of BM transcriptional factors, such as RUNX2 (Chen et al., 2021; Kim et al., 2020), C/EBPs (Wang et al., 2022), and PPARγ (Brunmeir and Xu, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2021; Kim et al., 2020.

claim: Thousands of intracellular proteins are dynamically modified by a single O-linked N-Acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) moiety at serine or threonine residues, termed O-GlcNAcylation.
source: Thousands of intracellular proteins are dynamically modified by a single O-linked N-Acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) moiety at serine or threonine residues, termed O-GlcNAcylation (Hart et al., 2007; Ruan et al., 2013b; Yang and Qian, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hart et al., 2007; Ruan et al., 2013b; Yang and Qian, 2017.

claim: O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT), using UDP-GlcNAc derived from the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway as the substrate, controls diverse biological processes such as gene transcription, protein stability, and cell signaling.
source: O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT), using UDP-GlcNAc derived from the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway as the substrate, controls diverse biological processes such as gene transcription, protein stability, and cell signaling (Hanover et al., 2012; Ruan et al., 2014; Ruan et al., 2012; Ruan et al., 2013a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hanover et al., 2012; Ruan et al., 2014; Ruan et al., 2012; Ruan et al., 2013a.

claim: In cell culture, O-GlcNAcylation promotes osteogenesis.
source: In cell culture, O-GlcNAcylation promotes osteogenesis (Kim et al., 2007; Nagel and Ball, 2014) and suppresses adipogenesis (Ji et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2007; Nagel and Ball, 2014.

claim: In cell culture, O-GlcNAcylation suppresses adipogenesis.
source: In cell culture, O-GlcNAcylation promotes osteogenesis (Kim et al., 2007; Nagel and Ball, 2014) and suppresses adipogenesis (Ji et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ji et al., 2012.

claim: Newborn Ogt cKO mice showed no obvious change in long bone formation.
source: Compared to Sp7GFP:Cre littermate controls, newborn Ogt cKO mice showed no obvious change in long bone formation (Figure 1B) but had a profound defect in the mineralization of flat bones of the calvaria (Figure 1C), suggesting impaired intramembranous ossification during the prenatal stage.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Newborn Ogt cKO mice had a profound defect in the mineralization of flat bones of the calvaria.
source: Compared to Sp7GFP:Cre littermate controls, newborn Ogt cKO mice showed no obvious change in long bone formation (Figure 1B) but had a profound defect in the mineralization of flat bones of the calvaria (Figure 1C), suggesting impaired intramembranous ossification during the prenatal stage.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The defect in calvaria mineralization in newborn Ogt cKO mice suggests impaired intramembranous ossification during the prenatal stage.
source: Compared to Sp7GFP:Cre littermate controls, newborn Ogt cKO mice showed no obvious change in long bone formation (Figure 1B) but had a profound defect in the mineralization of flat bones of the calvaria (Figure 1C), suggesting impaired intramembranous ossification during the prenatal stage.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed calvaria defect in Figure 1C.

claim: At 4–6 weeks of age, Ogt cKO mice were modestly shorter than the controls.
source: At 4–6 weeks of age, Ogt cKO mice were modestly shorter than the controls (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: Histological analyses showed decreased bone volume and osteoblast number in Ogt cKO mice.
source: Histological analyses showed decreased bone volume and osteoblast number (Figure 1F) and shortened growth plate (Figure 1G) in Ogt cKO mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Histological analyses showed shortened growth plate in Ogt cKO mice.
source: Histological analyses showed decreased bone volume and osteoblast number (Figure 1F) and shortened growth plate (Figure 1G) in Ogt cKO mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Micro-CT scanning showed that Ogt cKO mice had reduced trabecular bone volume, bone volume to tissue volume ratio, trabecular thickness, and trabecular numbers in the distal femur.
source: Micro-CT scanning further showed that Ogt cKO mice had reduced trabecular bone volume, bone volume to tissue volume ratio, trabecular thickness, and trabecular numbers in the distal femur (Figure 1H–L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H–L.

claim: Ogt cKO mice represent typical bone and dental defects as observed in Runx2-haploinsufficient mice.
source: Ogt cKO mice represent typical bone and dental defects (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) as observed in Runx2-haploinsufficient mice (Otto et al., 1997; Takarada et al., 2016), suggesting that O-GlcNAcylation might control RUNX2 function.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and citations to Otto et al., 1997; Takarada et al., 2016.

claim: The similarity between Ogt cKO mice and Runx2-haploinsufficient mice suggests that O-GlcNAcylation might control RUNX2 function.
source: Ogt cKO mice represent typical bone and dental defects (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) as observed in Runx2-haploinsufficient mice (Otto et al., 1997; Takarada et al., 2016), suggesting that O-GlcNAcylation might control RUNX2 function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the phenotypic similarity between Ogt cKO and Runx2-haploinsufficient mice.

claim: Alkaline phosphatase staining revealed a reduction in mineralization of Ogt cKO BMSCs.
source: Alkaline phosphatase staining revealed a reduction in mineralization of Ogt cKO BMSCs (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Treating mesenchymal C3H10T1/2 cells with an OGT inhibitor, OSMI-1, reduced mineralization after osteogenic differentiation.
source: Similarly, treating mesenchymal C3H10T1/2 cells with an OGT inhibitor, OSMI-1, reduced mineralization (Figure 2B) and ablated calcium deposition (Figure 2C) after osteogenic differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Treating mesenchymal C3H10T1/2 cells with OSMI-1 ablated calcium deposition after osteogenic differentiation.
source: Similarly, treating mesenchymal C3H10T1/2 cells with an OGT inhibitor, OSMI-1, reduced mineralization (Figure 2B) and ablated calcium deposition (Figure 2C) after osteogenic differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is a bone anabolic agent that requires RUNX2-dependent signaling.
source: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is a bone anabolic agent that requires RUNX2-dependent signaling (Krishnan et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Krishnan et al., 2003.

claim: PTH treatment of C3H10T1/2 cells increased global protein O-GlcNAcylation.
source: We found that PTH treatment of C3H10T1/2 cells increased global protein O-GlcNAcylation (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The ability of PTH to activate osteogenesis is completely abolished when OGT was inhibited by OSMI-1.
source: The ability of PTH to activate osteogenesis is completely abolished when OGT was inhibited by OSMI-1 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Pharmacological activation of O-GlcNAcylation enhances RUNX2 activity and promotes osteogenic differentiation.
source: Pharmacological activation of O-GlcNAcylation enhances RUNX2 activity and promotes osteogenic differentiation (Kim et al., 2007; Nagel and Ball, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2007; Nagel and Ball, 2014.

claim: RUNX2 is O-GlcNAcylated at Ser 32, Ser 33, and Ser 371.
source: We mutated three known O-GlcNAc sites on RUNX2, Ser 32 and Ser 33 in the N-terminal transactivation domain and Ser 371 in the proline/serine/threonine-rich domain (Figure 2F), to alanine (3A), and found that mutant RUNX2 possessed less O-GlcNAcylation (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F and 2G.

claim: Mutant RUNX2 (3A) possessed less O-GlcNAcylation than wildtype RUNX2.
source: We mutated three known O-GlcNAc sites on RUNX2, Ser 32 and Ser 33 in the N-terminal transactivation domain and Ser 371 in the proline/serine/threonine-rich domain (Figure 2F), to alanine (3A), and found that mutant RUNX2 possessed less O-GlcNAcylation (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: OGA inhibition by Thiamet-G (TMG) increased O-GlcNAcylation of wildtype (WT) RUNX2, but to a much less extent in the 3A mutant.
source: O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition by Thiamet-G (TMG) increased O-GlcNAcylation of wildtype (WT) RUNX2, but to a much less extent in the 3A mutant (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: OGT inhibition by OSMI-1 or O-GlcNAc mutation both impaired the transcriptional activity of RUNX2 on a luciferase reporter.
source: OGT inhibition by OSMI-1 or O-GlcNAc mutation both impaired the transcriptional activity of RUNX2 on a luciferase reporter (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: OSMI-1 could still suppress luciferase activity of RUNX2-3A, suggesting additional, unidentified O-GlcNAc sites.
source: OSMI-1 could still suppress of luciferase activity of RUNX2-3A (Figure 2H), suggesting additional, unidentified O-GlcNAc sites (Figure 2G), which requires future investigation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: When overexpressed in C3H10T1/2 cells, RUNX2-3A substantially lost the ability to induce osteogenic differentiation.
source: Nevertheless, when overexpressed in C3H10T1/2 cells, RUNX2-3A substantially lost the ability to induce osteogenic differentiation (Figure 2I) or RUNX2-target gene expression (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: When overexpressed in C3H10T1/2 cells, RUNX2-3A substantially lost the ability to induce RUNX2-target gene expression.
source: Nevertheless, when overexpressed in C3H10T1/2 cells, RUNX2-3A substantially lost the ability to induce osteogenic differentiation (Figure 2I) or RUNX2-target gene expression (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: O-GlcNAcylation is essential for RUNX2 activity and osteogenesis.
source: These data demonstrate that O-GlcNAcylation is essential for RUNX2 activity and osteogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: In adult mice, Sp7 expression is restricted to osteoblast precursors.
source: In adult mice, Sp7 expression is restricted to osteoblast precursors.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Adult-onset deletion of OGT in Sp7+ cells resulted in reduced bone volume, trabecular thickness, and bone mineral density.
source: Micro-CT showed that Ogt cKO mice had reduced bone volume, trabecular thickness, and bone mineral density (Figure 3B–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B–E.

claim: OGT is functionally indispensable in the committed osteolineage for adult trabecular bone remodeling.
source: Together, these results support the functional indispensability of OGT in the committed osteolineage for adult trabecular bone remodeling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the adult-onset deletion experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: The osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation of BMSCs is generally considered mutually exclusive.
source: The osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation of BMSCs is generally considered mutually exclusive (Ambrosi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ambrosi et al., 2017.

claim: Concomitant with bone loss, a massive accumulation of adipocytes was observed in the bone marrow of Ogt cKO mice.
source: Concomitant with bone loss, we observed a massive accumulation of adipocytes in the bone marrow of Ogt cKO mice, shown by hematoxylin & eosin staining (Figure 4A) and immune-staining of the lipid droplet protein – perilipin (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Pdgfrα and Vcam1 (encoding CD106) have been recently identified as surface markers of adipogenic lineage cells in the BM that also express the Lepr and Adipoq genes.
source: Pdgfrα and Vcam1 (encoding CD106) have been recently identified as surface markers of adipogenic lineage cells in the BM that also express the Lepr and Adipoq genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; Baryawno et al., 2019; Zhong et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Baryawno et al., 2019; Zhong et al., 2020 and data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Flow cytometric analysis revealed that Ogt cKO mice possessed more PDGFRα+VCAM1+ adipogenic progenitors than littermate controls.
source: Flow cytometric analysis of BMSCs revealed that Ogt cKO mice possessed more PDGFRα+VCAM1+ adipogenic progenitors than littermate controls (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Adipogenic differentiation of primary BMSCs showed increased lipid deposition in Ogt cKO mice.
source: To directly test if OGT deficiency biases BMSC differentiation toward the adipogenic lineage, we first induced the adipogenic differentiation of primary BMSCs and found increased lipid deposition in Ogt cKO mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Under osteogenic induction conditions, adipo-lineage markers such as Adipoq and Vcam1 were significantly upregulated by OGT deficiency.
source: Even under an osteogenic induction condition, adipo-lineage markers such as Adipoq and Vcam1 were significantly upregulated by OGT deficiency (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: Treating C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal cells with an OGA inhibitor TMG to increase protein O-GlcNAcylation substantially reduced perilipin protein expression.
source: Furthermore, treating C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal cells with an OGA inhibitor TMG to increase protein O-GlcNAcylation, was able to substantially reduce perilipin protein expression (Figure 4G) and Pparg and Adipoq gene expression (Figure 4H, I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Treating C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal cells with TMG substantially reduced Pparg and Adipoq gene expression.
source: Furthermore, treating C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal cells with an OGA inhibitor TMG to increase protein O-GlcNAcylation, was able to substantially reduce perilipin protein expression (Figure 4G) and Pparg and Adipoq gene expression (Figure 4H, I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4H and I.

claim: OGT inhibits the adipogenic program of BMSCs.
source: These data indicate that OGT inhibits the adipogenic program of BMSCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: C/EBPβ is an early transcription factor that specifies the adipogenic fate of BMSCs.
source: We then looked to C/EBPβ, an early transcription factor that specifies the adipogenic fate of BMSCs (Cao et al., 1991; Darlington et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cao et al., 1991; Darlington et al., 1998.

claim: OGT modifies C/EBPβ to inhibit its transcriptional activity.
source: It has been reported that OGT modifies C/EBPβ to inhibit its transcriptional activity (Li et al., 2009; Qian et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2009; Qian et al., 2018.

claim: Ablating O-GlcNAcylation of C/EBPβ (2A mutation) promotes adipogenic differentiation of C3H10T1/2 cells.
source: As expected, ablating O-GlcNAcylation of C/EBPβ (2A mutation) promotes adipogenic differentiation of C3H10T1/2 cells (Figure 4J and K).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4J and K.

claim: By O-GlcNAcylating and reciprocally regulating RUNX2 and C/EBPβ, OGT is required for the proper allocation of skeletal progenitors into osteogenic versus adipogenic lineages during development.
source: Taken together, we concluded that, by O-GlcNAcylating and reciprocally regulating RUNX2 and C/EBPβ, OGT is required for the proper allocation of skeletal progenitors into osteogenic versus adipogenic lineages during development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Skeletal development is concomitant with the establishment of definitive hematopoiesis in the BM.
source: Skeletal development is concomitant with the establishment of definitive hematopoiesis in the BM.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: No changes in the percentage of lineage-Sca-1+Kit+ (LSK) progenitor cells, common lymphoid progenitors (CLPs), or Fraction A that contains pre-pro-B cells were observed between control and Ogt cKO mice.
source: No changes in the percentage of lineage-Sca-1+Kit+ (LSK) progenitor cells, common lymphoid progenitors (CLPs), Fraction A that contains pre-pro-B cells were observed between control and Ogt cKO mice (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B–D.

claim: Frequencies of Fraction B and C pro-B, pre-B, and immature B in Ogt cKO mice were drastically reduced.
source: While frequencies of Fraction B and C pro-B, pre-B, and immature B in Ogt cKO mice were drastically reduced (Figure 5E–I), demonstrating a developmental blockage from pre-pro-B to pro-B cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E–I.

claim: Ogt cKO mice demonstrate a developmental blockage from pre-pro-B to pro-B cells.
source: While frequencies of Fraction B and C pro-B, pre-B, and immature B in Ogt cKO mice were drastically reduced (Figure 5E–I), demonstrating a developmental blockage from pre-pro-B to pro-B cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 5E–I.

claim: In the peripheral blood, there was specific loss of CD19+B220+ B cells but not CD4+ or CD8+ T cells in Ogt cKO mice.
source: In the peripheral blood, there was specific loss of CD19+B220+ B cells but not CD4+ or CD8+ T cells (Figure 5J–L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5J–L.

claim: B-cell dysfunction observed in Ogt cKO mice was similar to the phenotype in mice when all Sp7+ cells were depleted.
source: B-cell dysfunction observed here was similar to the phenotype in mice when all Sp7+ cells were depleted (Yu et al., 2016) or IL-7 was deleted in BMSCs (Cordeiro Gomes et al., 2016), indicating that O-GlcNAcylation is essential for the Sp7+ lineage cells to establish a niche environment for B-cell lymphopoiesis.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yu et al., 2016.

claim: B-cell dysfunction observed in Ogt cKO mice was similar to the phenotype in mice when IL-7 was deleted in BMSCs.
